SCHEME OF WORK FOR PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
GRADE 7 — TERM 3
SCHOOL: ___________________________ | SCHOOL: ___________________________ | TEACHER: ___________________________ | TEACHER: ___________________________
GRADE: 7 | GRADE: 7 | TERM: 3 | TERM: 3
Wk | Lsn | Strand | Sub-Strand | Specific Learning Outcomes | Suggested Learning Experiences | Key Inquiry Question(s) | Learning Resources | Assessment | Reflection
1 | 1-4 | REVISION & REPORTING | Opening of School, Reporting & Administration | By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
a) Report to school and settle into learning activities.
b) Issue, verify, and clean technical drawing tools and workshop equipment.
c) Review Term 2 performance and set academic targets for Term 3. | • Learners report to school, clean and organize the Pre-Technical laboratory/classroom.
• Issue drawing sets, textbooks, and logbooks.
• Teacher guides learners through review of Term 2 evaluation papers and goal setting. | How does proper preparation set the stage for academic success in Term 3? | Logbooks, Drawing sets, KLB Top Scholar Pre-Technical Grade 7, Past revision papers | Checklist, Student self-assessment, Inventory review |
2 | 1-2 | 4.0 Tools & Fasteners | 4.1 Hand Tools | By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
a) Identify common marking and measuring tools used in technical workshops.
b) Demonstrate proper use of measuring tapes, steel rules, and try squares.
c) Care for measuring tools. | • Learners examine measuring tools (steel rules, tape measures, try squares).
• Practice measuring and marking given timber and metal specimens accurately. | Why is accuracy crucial when taking measurements in technical projects? | Steel rules, Measuring tapes, Try squares, Marking gauges, Workpieces | Practical observation, Measurement accuracy test |
2 | 3-4 | 4.0 Tools & Fasteners | 4.1 Hand Tools (Cutting & Shaping) | By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
a) Identify cutting and shaping tools (handsaws, chisels, files).
b) Demonstrate safe cutting operations.
c) Value tool maintenance. | • Learners observe cutting tools and practice safe sawing and filing techniques under supervision.
• Practice cleaning and oiling tools after use. | How do correct cutting tools improve efficiency and safety? | Handsaws, Wood chisels, Flat files, Workbenches, Safety goggles | Practical task assessment, Observation |
3 | 1-2 | 4.0 Tools & Fasteners | 4.2 Fasteners & Joining | By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
a) Identify common temporary and permanent fasteners (screws, nails, bolts, rivets).
b) Select appropriate fasteners for wood and metal joining. | • Learners examine samples of nails, wood screws, bolts, nuts, and pop rivets.
• Practice joining wood pieces using wood screws and screwdrivers. | What factors determine the choice of a fastener in construction? | Nails, Screws, Bolts, Screwdrivers, Spanners, Wood samples | Hands-on demonstration, Product evaluation |
3 | 3-4 | 5.0 Entrepreneurship & Energy | 5.1 Introduction to Entrepreneurship | By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
a) Explain the meaning of entrepreneurship and an entrepreneur.
b) Identify business opportunities in technical fields within the locality. | • Learners brainstorm local technical enterprises (welding, carpentry, computer repair, tailoring).
• Discuss qualities of a successful entrepreneur. | How can technical skills be transformed into viable business enterprises? | Case studies of local entrepreneurs, Textbooks, Resource person | Oral questioning, Group presentation |
4 | 1-2 | 5.0 Entrepreneurship & Energy | 5.2 Forms of Energy | By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
a) Define energy and state its primary forms (electrical, solar, mechanical, chemical).
b) Distinguish between renewable and non-renewable energy sources. | • Learners identify local energy sources (solar panels, mains electricity, firewood, wind).
• Classify sources into renewable and non-renewable in chart groups. | Why is the transition to renewable energy essential for sustainability? | Solar panel models, Energy classification charts, Multimedia slides | Written tasks, Peer evaluation |
4 | 3-4 | 5.0 Entrepreneurship & Energy | 5.3 Energy Transformation | By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
a) Explain energy transformation principles.
b) Construct simple energy transformation setups (e.g., solar to electrical to light). | • Learners set up simple circuits using small solar cells, wires, switch, and LED bulbs to demonstrate energy conversion. | How is energy converted from one form to another in everyday appliances? | Solar cells, Connecting wires, LED bulbs, Small DC motors, Dry cells | Practical experiment check, Group report |
5 | 1-2 | 6.0 Simple Mechanisms | 6.1 Levers and Linkages | By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
a) Explain the concept of a simple mechanism.
b) Classify levers into 1st, 2nd, and 3rd order levers with local examples. | • Learners operate common levers (prying tools, wheelbarrows, tweezers, scissors).
• Identify effort, fulcrum, and load positions for each class. | How do simple levers reduce the effort needed to perform heavy work? | Scissors, Pliers, Wheelbarrow model, Tweezers, Diagrams of levers | Practical classification task, Short written test |
5 | 3-4 | 6.0 Simple Mechanisms | 6.2 Pulleys and Gears | By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
a) Identify simple pulley systems and gear trains.
b) Demonstrate how pulleys and gears transmit motion and force. | • Learners observe pulley systems (flagpole, crane models) and interlocking toy gears to observe direction and speed of rotation. | Where are gears and pulleys applied in daily transportation and machinery? | Pulley models, Ropes, Gear sets/bicycle gears, Charts | Observation checklist, Oral feedback |
6 | 1-4 | 7.0 Practical Project Work | 7.1 Design & Fabrication Project | By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
a) Design a simple technical artifact (e.g., wooden pencil holder or key rack).
b) Apply safety, measurement, cutting, and joining skills to fabricate the artifact. | • Learners draft simple orthographic/pictorial sketches of chosen project.
• Measure, cut, join, and finish artifacts using available workshop materials. | How do design principles guide the creation of useful functional items? | Timber off-cuts, Hand tools, Fasteners, Sandpaper, Varnish, Drawing sheets | Project assessment rubrics, Portfolio review |
7 | 1-4 | REVISION & ASSESSMENT | 7.2 End-of-Year Assessment Preparation | By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
a) Consolidate key technical concepts learned across Terms 1, 2, and 3.
b) Complete end-of-term assessment papers with confidence. | • Learners tackle topical revision quizzes and past assessment papers in pairs.
• Teacher reviews troublesome areas in drawing, safety, tools, and energy. | Which technical concepts require further practice and mastery? | Past assessment papers, Revision guidebooks, Model answers | Summative end-of-term examinations |
8 | 1-4 | CLOSING & REPORTING | Week 8: Marking, Reporting & School Closing | By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to:
a) Receive evaluation feedback on practical projects and exams.
b) Clean and store workshop equipment securely for long vacation. | • Teacher marks, records, and issues report forms.
• Learners conduct complete workshop cleaning, stocktaking, and tool rust-proofing. | How do stocktaking and tool maintenance preserve school facilities? | Report books, Inventory register, Tool oil/grease, Storage cabinets | Inventory check, Closing activities |
